original_test_intent: Read the target ComputerSystem's supported PCIe collection representation and validate complete member/link/count identity while retaining only approved redacted topology evidence.
original_method: Resolve the System and its firmware-documented PCIe link, use trusted agent-host curl/jq to issue a bounded GET, validate collection type, count, unique device/function member links and required identity fields, then export redacted evidence.
manual_activity: The firmware/platform owner confirms the System PCIe representation and expected population/field policy, and the security owner approves exposure, retention and redaction of vendor/device IDs, addresses, serials and topology.
required_inputs: Advertised or firmware-documented PCIe collection link
Expected population and required identity-field policy
Trusted TLS and least-privilege credential provider
curl and jq on the approved agent host
safety_requirements: Reject unsupported or unlinked OEM aliases
Bound pagination and detect repeated links
Do not export unrestricted PCIe topology/serial data
No PCIe reset, hotplug, firmware, power or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Resolve System and approved PCIe representation
Capture status/headers and restricted raw hash
Validate resource type, count, unique links, pagination and required fields
Classify device versus function members where defined
Export approved redacted inventory and no-mutation audit

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: curl/jq on the agent host are appropriate, but a fixed `system` ID and direct `/PCIe` assumption do not prove resource identity. Pretty JSON lacks count, member type, duplicate/pagination and privacy validation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS, follow the selected System's approved PCIe link, require 2xx Redfish JSON, validate collection type/count/unique member links and bounded pagination, then export only approved redacted device/function identity metadata.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The PCIe collection GET and 15/10 timing remain; no SystemId, path portability, population, member type or inventory value is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the potentially OEM PCIe representation to firmware/schema evidence and validate collection completeness plus privacy controls before comparing inventory.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces fixed identity, unsafe access and raw pretty-printing with advertised-link/schema/count/pagination validation and controlled redaction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Establishes collection population and membership; individual member fields and broader PCIeDevices inventory remain separate testcases.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Management-plane PCIe inventory may lag host enumeration or omit functions; it cannot by itself prove link speed, lane width, driver binding or device functionality.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent if it preserves the selected System link, firmware representation, certificate binding, count/Members/pagination and redaction evidence. Host `lspci` may corroborate population but cannot replace this BMC endpoint contract.
expected_evidence: Immutable BMC/System identity and firmware/schema provenance
HTTP status/content type and restricted raw response hash
Collection type, count, unique device/function links and pagination audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item, path and GET consistently describe a PCIe collection read. Portability, fixed DeepSeek member identity and privacy omissions are implementation deficiencies, not contradictory Master semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The PCIe inventory purpose is clear. Firmware representation, schema/population, trust, access and privacy policy are concrete prerequisites.

review_improvement: Adds firmware-backed resource identity, collection completeness, member typing and sensitive topology redaction to an otherwise unvalidated JSON dump.
independent_technical_reasoning: The literal `PCIe` child is not enough to establish a portable collection contract; it may be an OEM aggregate, a link wrapper or unsupported on another firmware. Automation must prove the parent link and resource type before interpreting members, then validate counts, uniqueness and pagination so omissions are visible. Since PCIe IDs, addresses and topology can expose platform architecture, raw output requires restricted retention and a redacted comparison view.
